articles.what: Dark brown magnetic tape ribbon fragments interwoven with tiny clear plastic and colored label-ink slivers. Up close: A heap of shredded brown tape: curled glossy ribbons in chocolate and rust brown, scattered with clear plastic chips, tiny silver rings and a few red, blue and cream slivers. Ribbon strands are 3-8 px wide and loop around each other. Like a bin of ruined mixtapes. From a distance: Reads as dark chocolate-brown speckle with silver glints and a few red-blue dots; ribbons blur to a gritty brown. Measured spec (average): metal 89, roughness 80, coat 86. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, show car, gt / sports car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Flannel: Cassette Tape" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, doors, tailgate: broad areas show the curl detail
Avoid small trim where it reads as noise
Cream or white numbers with an outline read; brown or dark numbers vanish.
Big plain stripes or blocks in cream or orange: stay readable over the tape
Pairs well with: cream, orange, chrome, black.
pitfalls: Not plaid flannel: no check despite the shelf name
Not dirt or wood: ribbons curl and glint, they are plastic
Avoid: numbers over the flecks, next to other busy finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 89 (pearl-level metal), roughness 80 (satin gloss), clearcoat 86 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers over the flecks, next to other busy finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: big plain stripes or blocks in cream or orange: stay readable over the tape; a number plate: needed for legibility
Patterns to avoid: camo, weave or dots: noise on noise; fine line patterns: lost in the ribbons
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat panel: glossy inlay against the satin; matte band: calm area against the sparkle
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Extreme: Chain Link
articles.summary: Fine galvanised diamond-wire mesh, uniform grey with bright sparkle, no background scene behind it. Reads as a uniform mid-dark grey with a fine diagonal crosshatch; at thumbnail size the diamonds merge into a steely, industrial grey with a slight sparkle.
articles.what: Fine galvanized diamond-wire mesh without a background scene, tiny diamonds. Up close: Bright silver wire diamonds in a tight lattice laid over a dull dark-grey galvanized plate, with small round knuckle dots at each wire crossing and faint mottled scuffs in the gaps. Wire is crisp, a few pixels thick. From a distance: Reads as a uniform mid-dark grey with a fine diagonal crosshatch; at thumbnail size the diamonds merge into a steely, industrial grey with a slight sparkle. Measured spec (average): metal 153, roughness 106, coat 121. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.

how: Click the zone you want to change.

tips: Hood, doors and bumpers: broad panels show the lattice; good as a lower-body band

Small numbers get lost in the lattice; use big bold numbers in white or red with a black outline.
Hex or mesh perforation: only if the scale clearly differs, otherwise it muddies

pitfalls: Not carbon fibre: diamonds are open wire, silver on grey, not black twill
Not a perforated grille: no holes, plate is solid behind

articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the mesh, big dark areas in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: hex or mesh perforation: only if the scale clearly differs, otherwise it muddies; stripes or racing bands: broad flat colour over the mesh keeps the diamonds as texture

Scraps carry halftone dots, black diagonal hazard stripes, grungy ink texture and tiny staple marks. No readable letters. Up close: Hundreds of real-looking safety pins, each 15-30 px long, tossed in every direction over a near-black ground. Bright silver coils, clasps and wire loops catch the light while the pin bodies are dim grey; pins overlap and pile up with no gaps. From a distance: Reads as a very dark black-charcoal with a fine silver glitter of scratchy lines; the pins merge into sparkling steel dust on black. articles.title: Flannel: Corduroy Olive
articles.summary: Olive-green fine-wale corduroy in short patches of differently angled ribbing, flat matte cloth. Reads as a flat dark olive drab with a busy fine cross-hatch grain; no sheen, like army cloth or old couch fabric.
articles.what: Olive fine-wale corduroy in short differently oriented ribbed patches. Up close: Patches of fine parallel ribs, about 3-4 px apart, in olive green, each patch 30-60 px across and turned a different direction like a patchwork quilt. Between patches are fuzzy lighter yellow-olive seams that look frayed. From a distance: Reads as a flat dark olive drab with a busy fine cross-hatch grain; no sheen, like army cloth or old couch fabric. Measured spec (average): metal 5, roughness 185, coat 206. Shine: matte. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
